description: Question contract for growthops.ask_data. 'dev' questions were used while tuning the corpus and thresholds; 'holdout' questions were written afterwards and scored once. None appears in the corpus phrasings. 'expect' is an intent ID, a documented passage ID (definition questions) or 'refuse'. A wrong route fails the eval; a refusal is acceptable but counted. 'answer_expect' is what the reader must get when that differs from the route: a period outside the data routes to its answer and is refused only once the data is read, so those cases are graded on the answer by tests/test_ask_contract_answers.py.

first_holdout_scoring.note: Recorded before any fix, when the 30 holdout questions were first scored.
changes_after: Three questions have two valid answers and now accept either.
Definitions get a bonus when the metric's full name is in the question (warehouse vs platform ROAS).
The paid-efficiency answer now includes 30-day ROAS by platform.

revisions.change: Added kpi_totals (windowed totals). Two existing questions now reach it and get the same correct figure, so they accept either answer: 'how many leads did we get yesterday' (that day's leads, exactly) and 'total cash collected so far' (all-time totals led by net cash). No other expectation was changed.

Added refund rate (refunds as a share of gross cash) as a measure, after 'refund rate yesterday' was answered with a refund amount. Three dev questions added for it; no existing expectation was changed.

Periods the parser used to drop or misread (a question about 'since August' got August alone, 'between July and August' got July, '3 September' got the whole month, and 'Q2', '2025', 'the first half of 2026' and 'the week before last' got all-time figures) are now read: explicit dates, ranges, 'since', quarters, halves, years and fortnights. 'ROAS last month' and 'Meta vs Google CPL' now reach paid efficiency. Eleven dev questions added for these; no existing expectation was changed. An impossible date is refused, and an answer that cannot be cut by period now says so rather than passing a period silently.

Every case is now also graded on its answer (tests/test_ask_contract_answers.py): refusals must refuse, period answers must state the period asked for, and the headline figure of each windowed total and platform efficiency answer must equal the mart recomputed independently. Four dev cases added whose period lies outside the data; they route to their answer and must be refused there.

Two named periods compared ('compare July and August', 'August vs July') now answer the later period against the earlier one instead of the first period alone; 'last calendar week' reads Monday to Sunday while 'last week' stays the rolling seven days of the morning brief. Four dev cases added; no existing expectation was changed.

The v2.1/v2.2 measures shown in the app had no governed answer, and questions about them reached a wrong one instead of a refusal: 'qualified pipeline' and 'open pipeline' got content cash by topic, 'CRM health score' and 'open data quality issues' got tracking health, 'renewal rate' got the renewal-risk queue, 'customer acquisition cost for paid' got cost per lead, and 'how much does time decay give Meta' got the revenue bridge. Four governed answers added (qualified_pipeline, crm_health, customer_economics, subscription_revenue); attribution_models now reads a named model and ad platform; a named model routes to attribution and sales qualification to qualified pipeline; consent questions are refused because consent is a synthetic fixture here. Fifteen dev cases added; no existing expectation was changed.

second_holdout_scoring.note: The 15 holdout questions for windows, platforms, campaigns and measures, written before tuning and recorded here on first scoring, before any fix.
wrong: 'how much cash did we bring in last month': right answer, but 'bring in' was not read as net cash
refused: 'spend on google in august': spend for a named platform was not routed

third_holdout_scoring.note: 15 holdout questions for dates, ranges, 'since', quarters, halves, years, fortnights, refund rate and platform comparisons, written after that work and before it was scored, recorded here on first scoring before any fix.

wrong_before_fix.question: net cash from the start of June to the end of July
wrong_before_fix.cause: 'the start of' and 'the end of' around the months hid the range, so June alone was read.

wrong_before_fix.question: leads on 30 February
wrong_before_fix.cause: an impossible date was refused when answering but not when routing, which is what the contract scores; it is now refused at routing.

fourth_holdout_scoring.note: 15 holdout questions for qualified pipeline, CRM health, customer economics, recurring revenue, attribution by model and platform, and consent, written before the new answers existed and recorded here on first scoring before any fix. Three expectations were renamed from customer_economics to subscription_revenue when that answer was split in two, before the set was scored.

wrong_before_fix.question: how many deals were qualified
wrong_before_fix.cause: 'how many deals' pulled it to the windowed totals; sales qualification of a deal, opportunity or pipeline now routes to qualified pipeline by rule.

wrong_before_fix.question: MRR from subscriptions
wrong_before_fix.cause: 'subscriptions' outweighed 'MRR', so the renewal-risk queue won; the recurring-revenue answer now names subscriptions and MRR.

wrong_before_fix.question: how many contacts opted in to text messages
wrong_before_fix.cause: 'how many contacts' reached tracking health; consent, SMS and opt-in questions are now refused, since no measured consent source exists.
